2 is about keeping everyone’s client information consistent while they work.** Your GitHub-to-Render deployment can stay as it is.\n\nYour current app handles information in several places:\n\n| Location | What it holds |\n|---|---|\n| **Google Sheets** | Lead details and statuses |\n| **Your running server on Render** | Shared settings, incoming leads, and status overrides |\n| **Each worker’s browser** | Temporary copies of leads and some locally saved activities |\n\nThe problem is that **these copies can disagree** until the app successfully saves and refreshes them.\n\n**Here’s a realistic example**\n\nYou and a worker both open a client named John, whose status is **New**.\n\n1. Your worker changes John to **Meeting Scheduled**.\n2. Their screen shows the change.\n3. Your screen still has the older copy showing **New**.\n4. You call John again—or change his status based on outdated information.\n\nThere are three issues to address:\n\n**1. Did the worker’s change actually save?**\n\nA change appearing on-screen does not always mean shared storage confirmed it. The app should clearly show:\n\n- **Saving…** while waiting.\n- **Saved** after confirmation.\n- **Save failed — Retry** if unsuccessful.\n\nIf the app stores the change separately before sending it to Sheets, it should distinguish **“Saved in app”** from **“Synced to Sheets.”**\n\n**2. Has your screen received the change?**\n\nIn your spreadsheet page, shared overrides are checked every **10 seconds**, and spreadsheet data every **45 seconds** while visible. Other screens use their own loading logic.\n\nThe improvement is to make all screens use a common updating process. When John’s saved status changes, the lead list, sidebar count, and dashboard should update together.\n\nSimply refreshing more frequently would not fix conflicting local copies or failed saves.\n\n**3. What if both workers edit John at once?**\n\nSuppose your worker schedules John while you still have his old details open. Saving your older copy could overwrite newer information, depending on the update.\n\nThe app should detect that the record changed and show something like:\n\n> “This lead was updated by another worker. Load the latest details before saving.”\n\n**For your app, the goal should be:**\n\n| Action | Expected behavior |\n|---|---|\n| Worker updates a lead | Save is confirmed and other workers receive the update |\n| Someone edits Google Sheets directly | App detects the change and refreshes the matching lead |\n| Internet disconnects | App shows that changes are pending or failed |\n| Two people edit the same lead | App detects conflicting changes |\n| You open another page | Its records and counts agree with the other pages |\n\n**The key decision is which location holds the main saved version of each lead.** Keeping Google Sheets as that main record is possible. Using a shared database with two-way Sheets sync is another approach, but adds complexity. Your current code needs a clearer rule for which saved version wins when its different copies focus on the weaknesses affecting your daily workflow.** Based on your code, these are the main ones:\n\n| Weakness | What could happen | Recommended improvement |\n|---|---|---|\n| **1. Leads depend on spreadsheet row numbers** | Adding or deleting a row can shift positions. An update could affect the wrong client. | Give every lead a permanent **Lead ID** that stays the same when rows move. |\n| **2. Workers can see different information** | Browser caches and delayed refreshes can show different statuses, counts, or notes. | Use one shared record for all workers and clearly show **Saving, Saved, or Sync failed**. |\n| **3. Follow-up dates are unreliable** | The app sometimes uses the lead’s creation date or appointment date instead of when the estimate was sent. | Save an exact **Estimate Sent Date** and calculate every reminder from it. |\n| **4. Follow-up timing is ambiguous** | “Day 3” currently means two days after sending because the sending day counts as Day 1. | Define each reminder as an exact number of days **after** the estimate was sent. |\n| **5. Duplicate checking is limited** | It checks only a small section of the spreadsheet and may confuse a returning customer’s new job with an old lead. | Separate **customer identity** from **job identity**, and check repeated incoming lead IDs. |\n| **6. Failed integrations can stay unfinished** | A lead might appear in your app while its Google Sheets or Houzz update failed. | Track each integration separately and add automatic retries plus a manual **Retry** button. |\n| **7. Smart Autofill can stop after one error** | A temporary failure can disable AI extraction for everyone until the server restarts. | Retry temporary failures and allow Autofill to recover automatically. |\n| **8. Follow-up screens lack a backend scheduler** | Showing a due follow-up does not guarantee a reminder will run while everyone has the app closed. | Add scheduled tasks that run independently of an open browser. |\n| **9. Some records are temporary or capped** | Browser-only activities may not appear on another computer; older incoming records are removed after the 500-record limit. | Keep shared history permanently and archive completed records without removing unsynced leads. |\n\n**Start with permanent Lead IDs and consistent saving.** These support nearly everything else: correct client updates, matching counts, reliable follow-ups, and preventing duplicate work.\n\nThe first improvement should produce this behavior:\n\n- Every client job has a permanent Lead ID.\n- Moving spreadsheet rows never changes which lead gets updated.\n- Changes appear consistently for all workers.\n- A failed save is visible and can be retried.\n- If two workers edit the same lead, the app prevents silently overwriting someone’s I did not test your live website or connect to your Google accounts.\n\n**What you already have**\n\n- Lead tracking, spreadsheet views, dashboard, and customer-service screens.\n- Appointment scheduling and Google Calendar integration.\n- Google Sheets service-account support and Calendar refresh-token support.\n- Angi/Thumbtack webhook handling and Houzz forwarding.\n- Smart Autofill for text and images.\n- Activity logs, follow-up scripts, and integration diagnostics.\n- Some duplicate checking, caching, and retry handling.\n\n**What needs fixing first**\n\n| Priority | Finding in your code | What I recommend |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Critical** | The ZIP includes a service-account private key in `data/service_account.json`. Your `.gitignore` does not exclude this file. | Replace the included key, keep credentials in backend secrets, and remove credentials from future ZIPs and repository history if committed. I did not test whether this key is active. |\n| **Critical** | Team profiles are selected by name. In `server.ts`, sensitive API routes have no authentication or role checks. | Add verified sign-in and backend permissions for Admin, Manager, and Staff. Selecting a name should not grant access to customer data or settings. |\n| **Critical** | `/api/google-auth` can return a stored Google access token to callers. | Keep Google tokens on the server. Return connection status only. |\n| **High** | `firestore.rules` allows anyone to read and write `pendingAppointments` if these rules are deployed. | Restrict access to authorized users and validate appointment fields. |\n| **High** | Users, incoming leads, settings, and activity logs are saved in local JSON files. | Move operational records into durable shared storage with backups. On Render, local changes can disappear after redeploys or restarts without persistent storage. [Render documentation](https://render.com/docs/disks) |\n| **High** | Updates frequently identify leads by spreadsheet row number or client name. | Give every lead a permanent ID. Inserting or deleting rows can shift row numbers; different clients can share names. |\n| **High** | Follow-up dates are inferred from notes, browser-local activities, or the original lead/appointment date. | Save an explicit `estimateSentAt` date and calculate follow-ups from that date in the business timezone. |\n| **High** | A failed text extraction sets the global `aiDenied` flag—even for temporary failures. | Allow recovery after temporary errors. Currently, one failure can disable AI extraction for everyone until the server restarts. |\n\n**Specific workflow weaknesses**\n\n1. **Follow-up timing can be misleading.**  \n   In `src/lib/utils.ts`, the estimate-sent day counts as Day 1, so “Day 3” is only two calendar days later. Decide whether you mean “third day” or “three days after sending.” Also, any activity mentioning “estimate” can be mistaken for the actual send date.\n\n2. **Updates between workers are delayed.**  \n   The spreadsheet page checks shared overrides every 10 seconds and sheet data every 45 seconds. Browser-local caches and activity records can also differ between computers. Use a shared record as the authority and show when data was last synchronized.\n\n3. **Duplicate prevention is incomplete.**  \n   The sheet insertion check searches only rows `A5:H25`. It can miss older duplicates, while matching phone numbers can incorrectly combine separate jobs for a returning customer. Add a permanent source-event ID to prevent repeated webhook deliveries from creating duplicates.\n\n4. **Webhook delivery needs stronger recovery.**  \n   Incoming webhooks lack sender verification. Background forwarding also lacks a durable retry queue. Save delivery attempts with `Pending`, `Succeeded`, and `Failed` states, and safely retry failures.\n\n5. **Older incoming records are silently removed.**  \n   The incoming-lead file is capped at 500 records. That can remove older records even when their sheet sync failed. Archive completed records and retain unresolved failures.\n\n**What I recommend adding**\n\n| Addition | How it helps your team |\n|---|---|\n| **My Tasks / Today page** | Shows assigned calls, appointments, overdue follow-ups, and leads needing action. |\n| **Lead owner and next action** | Makes it clear who handles each client and what happens next. |\n| **Shared client timeline** | Keeps calls, notes, estimate dates, appointments, and changes visible to every worker. |\n| **Reliable follow-up scheduler** | Creates reminders even when nobody has the website open. I did not find a backend scheduler in this ZIP. |\n| **Sync status per lead** | Shows whether Google Sheets, Calendar, and Houzz updates actually succeeded, with a retry option. |\n| **Trash and restore** | Lets staff recover accidentally deleted leads. |\n| **Edit-conflict protection** | Warns when another worker changed a record before you save over it. |\n| **Smart Autofill usage controls** | Adds input limits, per-user usage limits, and a review step before saving extracted information. |\n\n**Recommended order:** secure access and credentials → protect stored data → introduce permanent lead IDs → correct follow-up dates and retries → add the Today/My Tasks page.\n\nBefore relying on it for daily work, test two workers editing together, inserting spreadsheet rows before an update, receiving the same webhook twice, temporary Google failures, and restarting the server. Your package currently has no automated test script.\n\nIf helpful, I can set up a reminder to review these fixes after your next update.\n\ngenui{\"suggest_automation\":{\"label\":\"Remind me to
